title: A day in Little River
summary: A working waterfront at the north end of the Strand, with dolphin cruises, fishing, a vineyard and quiet marsh trails
description: A one-day Little River, SC itinerary: the waterfront, dolphin cruises, fishing charters, Vereen Memorial Gardens, La Belle Amie Vineyard and rainy-day options, with practical planning notes.
intro: Little River sits at the very northern edge of the Grand Strand, close to the North Carolina line, on the Intracoastal Waterway. It started as a fishing village and still has the feel of one: boats at the docks, charter captains and a pace that is slower than the busy centers of Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach.

In our directory Little River is its own area, and it has a good mix of things to do on and near the water, plus a few indoor and family options. A day here pairs well with time at the beach in nearby Cherry Grove. This itinerary is built around the water, since that is what the village does best.

sections.h: Morning: get out on the water
p: Boat trips are the main reason to visit. Sea Thunder and Sea Screamer run narrated dolphin cruises of roughly an hour and a half to two hours. The boats run up the Intracoastal Waterway, past barrier islands and out through the jetty to look for wild bottlenose dolphins. The two boats board at different docks, so check the address on your booking before you leave.

If you would rather fish, Little River Fishing Fleet runs headboat trips from Little River Landing, including a long Gulf Stream day and a shorter half-day trip, along with inshore and private charters. Fine Catch Fishing Charters offers guided charters of several lengths on a smaller boat, which suits a family or a small group that wants a more personal trip. Book early for weekends and summer, and ask about what is provided and what to bring when you reserve.

Vereen Memorial Gardens is an Horry County park on the waterfront in Little River, with about three miles of nature trails and boardwalks. It is free to enter, a good place for a walk or for watching birds, and it has views over the marsh and the waterway. It is also a sensible break between a morning on the boat and an afternoon activity. Beach wheelchairs can be reserved through the county if anyone in your group needs one.

Little River is a good place to pick one activity rather than try to do everything. For families with younger kids, Tribal Island Tiki Adventure Golf has two themed courses with volcanoes, caverns and waterfalls, and it is the northernmost mini golf stop on the Strand. Teens and adults who like a bit more action can try Shark Wake Park, a cable wakeboard and water-ski park on the lake at the North Myrtle Beach Park and Sports Complex, where no gear or experience is needed.

For something more relaxed, La Belle Amie Vineyard is a small vineyard a few miles north of the beach and away from the Highway 17 traffic. It is known for muscadine wines under the Twisted Sisters label, with tastings among the vines. Its hours are seasonal, so call before you drive out.

Pin Point Indoor Pickleball and Golf is an indoor sports venue with pickleball courts and golf simulators, and it has a bar and kitchen on site, so a rainy afternoon does not have to be cancelled. It works for groups of mixed ages and abilities.

sections.h: Evening: out on the water, or home for the sunset
p: PonTiki runs party boat cruises on the Intracoastal Waterway with music and dancing. Public cruises last about two hours and the boats are for guests of drinking age, so it suits a group of adults better than a family trip. If that is not your style, the waterfront is a pleasant place to watch the sun go down before heading back.

list: Little River is roughly a half hour or more from central Myrtle Beach, depending on traffic. Highway 17 is the main road, and summer weekends can be slow.
Water-based trips depend on weather and tides. Ask about rain and wind policies when you book.
Several businesses here are small and seasonal. Always check dates and hours on their own sites before you drive out.
See our guides to the water and to the area's fishing options for more ideas, and the rainy weekend itinerary if the forecast is poor.
